cohort: The study included 17,905,699 deliveries of full term, live births in the United States from 2016-2021.
finding: Compared to White individuals, higher odds of maternal blood transfusion were found among American Indian and Alaska Native, Black, Filipino, Korean, and Pacific Islander individuals, persisting after adjustment for confounders.
mod_finding: Racial disparities in maternal blood transfusion varied substantially by mode of delivery, with Black patients having lower transfusion rates than White patients in most delivery modes, but a higher rate in cesarean deliveries without trial of labor.
